description: The pie chart visually represents the distribution of content categories across a dataset, likely used in the context of training or evaluating a multimodal large language model for video captioning. It is divided into 14 distinct slices, each labeled with a category and its corresponding percentage. The largest segment, colored orange, represents “People Blogs” at 17.2%. The second largest, green, is “Howto Style” at 9.7%, followed by “Entertainment” in purple at 13.9%. Other notable segments include “Education” (red, 8.7%), “Sports” (pink, 7.7%), and “Gaming” (gray, 6.4%). Smaller segments include “Film Animation” (brown, 4.6%), “Travel Events” (yellow, 4.6%), “Comedy” (cyan, 5.6%), “Science Technology” (blue, 6.4%), “News Politics” (light orange, 4.3%), “Pets Animals” (light green, 3.9%), “Autos Vehicles” (red-orange, 4.8%), and “Music” (light purple, 2.3%). The chart uses a variety of distinct colors for each category, with percentage values clearly labeled inside each slice, and no slice is exploded or emphasized visually beyond its proportional size. The categories appear to be arranged in a roughly descending order clockwise from the top, though not strictly sorted. This distribution suggests a diverse but unevenly sampled dataset, with a strong emphasis on personal and instructional content.
